title: end4-pC plugin manifest
description: A plugin is one folder holding a manifest.json. Add "$schema": "../../core/manifest.schema.json" as the first key for editor completion and validation. scripts/validate-plugin.sh checks a manifest against this file.

id.description: Must equal the folder name. Lowercase, digits and dashes.

version.description: Semver. Not enforced beyond the shape.

apiVersion.description: The plugin API this was written against. The shell refuses anything it does not implement; see apiVersion in core/PluginRegistry.qml.

description.description: One line. Longer than that makes the plugin list ragged.

icon.description: Material Symbol name for the plugin list. scripts/check-icons.sh validates these against the installed font - an unknown name is not an error at runtime, the font just renders the string.

enabledByDefault.description: Whether the plugin is on before the user has ever touched it.

requires.description: Conditions for the plugin to be offered at all. It appears greyed out with a reason where unsupported, rather than failing at runtime.

runtimeDeps.description: nixpkgs attribute names put on the shell's PATH. Resolved at build time by modules/home/quickshell/default.nix; a name that does not exist fails the rebuild rather than the plugin. Use packageOverrides there when the attribute name differs.

provides.description: What the plugin contributes. Every kind is optional; a plugin providing nothing is legal but does nothing.

settings.description: User-editable settings, rendered automatically in Settings -> Plugins and in any settings section. Read them as settings.<key> on a base type, or PluginConfig.of("id").<key> anywhere.

materialSymbol.description: A Material Symbols Rounded ligature name, e.g. battery_full. Not a file path.

qmlFile.description: Path to a .qml file, relative to the plugin folder.

barWidget.description: A widget the user can place in the bar. Its root should be a PluginBarWidget.

id.description: Also the layout token stored in the user's bar config. Reusing a built-in id replaces that built-in.

materialPill.description: Whether the bar paints its pill behind this widget.

multipleAllowed.description: May appear more than once in a layout.

zone.description: Where to place the widget the first time the plugin is enabled. Without this, enabling the plugin appears to do nothing until the user drags the widget in from Settings -> Bar. Applied once and recorded; removing it afterwards is respected.

zoneOrder.description: Order relative to other auto-placed widgets in the same zone.

desktopWidget.description: A draggable widget on the desktop. Its root should be a PluginDesktopCard (header, content, footer, resize, persistence) or a bare PluginBackgroundWidget.

id.description: Must match the widgetId the QML sets, or position and size are stored under a different key than they are read from.

enabledByDefault.description: Whether the widget is on the desktop as soon as the plugin is enabled.

quickToggle.description: A tile in the sidebar's quick settings. Inherit AndroidQuickToggleButton and it works in the classic panel too.

classicEntry.description: A different file for the classic panel. Omit to use the same one.

menu.description: Expanded panel shown when the tile's chevron is tapped.

settingsPage.description: A whole page in Settings with its own navigation entry. Prefer settingsSections unless the plugin really owns a page's worth of UI.

settingsSection.description: A section injected into an existing Settings page, so a plugin's settings sit next to the related built-in ones and disappear when it is switched off.

page.description: Host page name, matched case-insensitively. Pages that host sections: Interface, Bar, Desktop, Services, Appearance, Advanced.

launcherAction.description: A static entry in the launcher, matched by name. For answering queries dynamically use searchProviders instead.

script.description: A script inside the plugin folder, run instead of exec. Anything typed after the action name is appended as arguments.

searchProvider.description: A live query handler in the launcher: a calculator, a converter, a dictionary, a note search. Its root must be a PluginSearchProvider. Fields here override the QML's own defaults.

prefix.description: Only consulted for queries starting with this. Empty means every query - correct only for a provider that can tell from the query itself whether it applies.

order.description: Lower sorts this provider's block of results earlier.

contextMenuItem.description: A row in the desktop right-click menu. Exactly one of ipc, exec or entry decides what it does.

order.description: Position among all rows. Built-ins sit at 10 (Wallpaper), 20 (Widgets), 30 (DropShelf), 40 (Live Wallpaper) and 100 (Settings).

entry.description: A submenu the plugin draws itself, opened on hover.

osdIndicator.description: A HUD shown over everything and dismissed on a timer: a countdown, a progress bar, a status flash. Show it with OsdRegistry.show("id"). The QML draws content only; the shell owns the window, placement and timeout.

timeout.description: Milliseconds. 0 uses the user's configured OSD timeout.

shortcut.description: A keybind, registered as the compositor global quickshell:<id>. The shell never edits the compositor config - `qs -c end4-pC ipc call plugins shortcuts` prints the exact line to paste.

suggestedKey.description: Compositor syntax, e.g. "SUPER SHIFT, B". A suggestion printed to the user, not something the shell binds.

ipcCall.description: Calls a function on a PluginIpc, in-process. Cheaper and more capable than spawning a command.

target.description: The PluginIpc's target, which defaults to the plugin id.

argv.description: A command as a list, never a shell string: ["notify-send", "hi"]. Each element is one argument, so nothing in it is ever interpreted by a shell.

appearanceColor.description: A colour role name understood by Appearance.getColorFromName.

key.description: Becomes a QML property, so it must be a valid identifier and cannot be a QML reserved word (data, children, parent, objectName, state, visible, enabled...). PluginConfig refuses and warns about the ones that would not work.

label.description: Shown next to the control. Defaults to the key.

placeholder.description: Greyed hint inside an empty text field. string type only.

group.description: Settings sharing a group are rendered as one titled block, in the order the groups first appear. Ungrouped settings come first.

default.description: Required in practice: a setting with no default reads as an empty value of its type.

options.description: enum only. Either plain strings, or { value, label } for a nicer control.
